task: End-to-end weighted proof transfer for the family-271 anisotropic Heisenberg spherical-law candidate, plus quantitative observable consequence and interface gate
overall_verdict: An internally reconstructed proof transfer supports the anisotropic spherical magnetization law for fixed positive spatial nearest-neighbor couplings, conditional on correctness of the explicitly audited source proof blocks. The transfer substitutions now cover conditioned exchange cycles, sparse pins, Sections 4-5, translation-invariant variational arguments, weighted pressure tangents, and SU(2) total-spin concentration. This is not external validation of the source or a priority claim. Combining the transfer with the pinned anisotropic Bloch-law companion gives a one-axis zero-field asymptotic for the determinant of the spin-stiffness tensor. There is no finite-volume bias rate, so no finite-specimen certification is supplied.

claims.exact_statement: Fix spin S in {1/2,1,3/2,...} and fixed J_1,J_2,J_3>0. For H_{S,L,J}=-sum_{x in (Z/LZ)^3} sum_{i=1}^3 J_i S_x dot S_{x+e_i} on even periodic cubes, let p_{S,beta,J}(h)=lim_{L even to infinity}(beta L^3)^(-1)log Tr exp[-beta(H_{S,L,J}-h M_L^3)] and m_{S,beta,J}=p'_{S,beta,J}(0+), with volume limit before field derivative. The family-271 proof transfers to show that for every fixed beta above a finite threshold beta_0(S,J), m>0, <exp[(t dot M_L)/L^3]> converges to sinh(m|t|)/(m|t|) for every t in R^3, and (L^3)^(-2)sum_{x,y}<S_x dot S_y> tends to m^2.
assumptions: Each J_i is fixed and strictly positive with finite J_max and positive J_min; each spatial bond couples the full spin scalar product.
S is fixed and positive half-integer; beta is fixed finite after beta_0(S,J) is chosen; L tends to infinity through even values.
The directional couplings are constant over the lattice, preserving translation invariance; no spin-space anisotropy or field is included in the zero-field conclusion.

The transfer uses the pinned source's finite pin/determinant, deterministic lattice Nash/flow, sparse-pin, zero-free, replica pressure, and total-spin arguments; those source arguments have not been externally validated.
claims.status: internally reconstructed end-to-end proof transfer modulo the source's base proof blocks; not external proof validation and no priority claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The pinned spherical-law theorem is equal-coupling nearest-neighbor only; the companion Bloch-law paper permits anisotropic finite-range interactions but does not prove spherical concentration. Complete-graph spherical transform and conditional loop-soup antecedents exist. Targeted search found no independent anisotropic lattice spherical-law theorem, but priority remains UNKNOWN. The source verification record has no independent build or expert review.
claims.costs: Theorem cost is an asymptotic Gibbs model with beta fixed then L to infinity; it supplies no explicit L_0(epsilon) or finite-volume law bias. A material test needs S, T, each J_i, zero-field calibration, independently equilibrated specimens, and one total-spin measurement per specimen or L^3 local readouts. Equilibration time, boundary/nonexchange error, instrument precision, finite-size bias and money remain UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the weighted next-pin/conditioned-cycle identities, sparse-pin exponents, weighted Section-5 block estimate, pressure-tangent Laplacian cancellation, or SU(2) total-spin endpoint under fixed positive directional weights falsifies this transfer. If any J_i=0, the proof's ellipticity fails and lower-dimensional layers can violate positive-temperature ordering.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert or formal verification of the base family-271 proof blocks; a complete priority search; and, for physical certification, a finite-size Wasserstein/modulus bound plus measured S,J_i,T, residual field, boundaries, and equilibration protocol.

claims.exact_statement: Conditional on the anisotropic spherical-law transfer and the pinned family-271 Bloch-law companion, for J(+-e_i)=J_i>0 one has Law(X_L) tending to Uniform[-m_{S,J}(beta),m_{S,J}(beta)] for X_L=M_L^3/L^3; hence E X_L^2 tends to m^2/3 and E X_L^4/(E X_L^2)^2 tends to 9/5. Since D_{S,J}=S diag(J_1,J_2,J_3), lim_{beta to infinity} beta^(3/2)[S-sqrt(3 lim_{L to infinity} E X_L^2)] = zeta(3/2)/(8 pi^(3/2) S^(3/2) sqrt(J_1 J_2 J_3)).
assumptions: Same model, coupling, limit order, and source-status assumptions as ANISO-HEISENBERG-SPHERICAL-LAW-TRANSFER.
Use the pinned anisotropic Bloch-law theorem with symmetric finite-range kernel J(+-e_i)=J_i and its thermodynamic-limit-before-beta limit order.
X_L is one self-adjoint component measurement; no joint finite-volume measurement of noncommuting spin components is used.
claims.status: exact asymptotic consequence of the conditional spherical-law transfer and source-reported Bloch-law companion; no finite-volume rate or experimental validation
claims.novelty_boundary: The Bloch coefficient is in the source companion and the spherical law is the transferred result. Their one-axis zero-field determinant formula is a direct asymptotic combination, not a separately validated experimental law. No finite-L or finite-beta remainder is supplied.
claims.costs: With R independent ideal equilibrium draws, mhat=2 mean |X_L| has sampling error eta at confidence 1-delta for R>=2 S^2 eta^(-2) log(2/delta); systematic finite-L bias is unknown. To resolve the beta^(-3/2) deficit, statistical and readout error must be o(beta^(-3/2)), implying R=O(beta^3) times accuracy/confidence factors; temperature and J calibration, field suppression beta L^3 |h|->0, boundary and equilibration costs remain uncharged/UNKNOWN.
claims.falsifier: A verified violation of one-axis uniform weak convergence or of the cited Bloch coefficient under the stated positive coupling convention falsifies the combined prediction. Finite specimen deviations alone do not falsify the asymptotic statement without a known rate.
claims.next_gate: Obtain W_1(Law(X_L),Uniform[-m,m])<=r_{S,beta,J}(L) and a parameter modulus for m; then combine them with measured S,T,J_i and an independently audited equilibration/readout protocol for a finite-size certificate.

claims.exact_statement: For the finite-volume SU(2)-invariant Gibbs state, let Y_L=J_L/L^3 and X_L=M_L^3/L^3. Then W1(Law(X_L),Uniform[-m,m]) <= L^-3 + (1/2) E|Y_L-m| and E[X_L^2]=E[J_L(J_L+1)]/(3L^6). The source nested partition proof supplies a symbolic lower-radius second-moment error C_{S,theta,rho}/log R_* + C(1+log log L)exp(-c sqrt(L)) + delta_loc(L,R_*), where delta_loc->0 only qualitatively at fixed R_*. The pressure upper tail has a finite-torus boundary error beta S(S+1)(J1+J2+J3)/L, but depends on an existential pressure-secant scale h_epsilon. Equations (7)-(9) of finite_volume_rate_gate.md combine these into a conditional W1/second-moment bound.
assumptions: Fixed S, beta, and strictly positive spatial couplings J_i; beta above the transferred ordering threshold.
The anisotropic Section 5 proof transfer and family-271 base source arguments are valid.
To instantiate a numerical finite-volume rate, explicit upper bounds on delta_loc(L,R_*) and a positive lower choice of h_epsilon are additionally required.
claims.status: derived conditional finite-volume interface; not an explicit rate or specimen certification because delta_loc and h_epsilon are unbounded by the source
claims.novelty_boundary: The grid-to-uniform conversion and finite pressure boundary estimate are elementary; the source does not quantify the finite-volume equilibrium approach or field-secant modulus. No claim of a new finite-size theorem or priority is made.
claims.costs: Finite-size partition scale contributes C/log R_* and an exponential telescoping term; numerical weighted constants, delta_loc, h_epsilon, equilibration and material calibration remain unavailable.
claims.falsifier: A verified counterexample to the fixed-parameter sphere law or failure of the weighted transfer falsifies the conditional interface; it does not claim a rate for which no finite data are given.
claims.next_gate: Prove an explicit finite-torus local-equilibrium stability modulus for the terminal blocks and an explicit pressure derivative modulus h_epsilon, then insert them into the displayed W1 bound.
